request: features: pr.list, pr.read, pr.line_items, pr.partial_selection, pr.status, pr.to_event, pr.partial_closure

skipped.title: Empty line_items array is rejected with code 2
Quantity above open quantity plus tolerance is rejected with 557

checkResults.scenario: PR list page 1 returns the documented envelope
checkResults.expectedResult: HTTP 200 from PurchaseRequests::ViewService. Default page size is 50. closure_configuration mirrors CustomConfiguration is_pr_partial_closure_enabled. No DB writes.
steps: 1. GET /purchase_requests with page=1 and a status filter
2. Assert HTTP 200
3. Assert keys purchase_requests, total_pages, total_pr_count, columns_configuration, closure_configuration
4. Assert each purchase_request carries rfq_no and a line_items array with the four quantity fields
checkResults.preconditions: Workspace has at least one PurchaseRequest not in status in_active with line items.

checkResults.scenario: PR list page=0 collapses to page 1
checkResults.expectedResult: HTTP 200. PurchaseRequests::SearchQuery sets @page = [1, params[:page].to_i].max, so 0, negative and non-numeric all resolve to page 1.
steps: 1. GET /purchase_requests?page=1 and record the PR uuid list
2. GET /purchase_requests?page=0
3. Assert both return the same first-page payload
checkResults.preconditions: Workspace has more than 50 PR line items so page 1 and page 2 differ.

checkResults.scenario: PR list far-out page returns an empty page with a real total_pages
checkResults.expectedResult: HTTP 200, empty purchase_requests. Kaminari yields an empty relation; total_pages must remain the true page count.
steps: 1. GET /purchase_requests?page=999999 with a status filter
2. Assert HTTP 200
3. Assert purchase_requests is empty
4. Assert total_pages and total_pr_count still describe the full result set
checkResults.preconditions: Workspace has fewer than 999999 pages of PR items.

checkResults.scenario: ageing_status=breach returns only items aged at or beyond the breach threshold
checkResults.expectedResult: HTTP 200. filter_by_ageing_status applies AGEING_DAYS_EXPR >= AGEING_BREACH_THRESHOLD (7). 'warning' is the 4..6 band.
steps: 1. GET /purchase_requests with ageing_status breach
2. Assert HTTP 200
3. Assert every returned line item reports ageing_in_days >= 7
4. Assert items younger than 4 days are absent
checkResults.preconditions: Config purchase_request_ageing_enabled is ON. Workspace has PR items older than 7 days with no PO, plus items younger than 4 days.

checkResults.scenario: Unrecognised ageing_status value is ignored instead of erroring
checkResults.expectedResult: HTTP 200. The case/else branch logs 'Unrecognized filter' and adds no condition, so the original relation is returned unfiltered.
steps: 1. GET /purchase_requests with an unknown ageing_status value
2. Assert HTTP 200 and a result set equal to the unfiltered active list
checkResults.preconditions: Config purchase_request_ageing_enabled is ON.

checkResults.scenario: is_dormant filter returns only PRs past the dormant threshold and not yet unlocked
checkResults.expectedResult: HTTP 200. The scope dormant_locked_for_company requires status active, dormant_unlocked_at IS NULL and CURRENT_DATE - created_at::date >= threshold.
steps: 1. GET /purchase_requests with is_dormant true
2. Assert HTTP 200
3. Assert the old locked PR is present
4. Assert the newer PR and the already-unlocked PR are absent
checkResults.preconditions: Config pr_dormant_threshold_days has a value > 0. Workspace has a PR older than the threshold with dormant_unlocked_at NULL, one newer PR, and one already unlocked.

checkResults.scenario: is_dormant filter is a no-op when the dormant feature is not configured
checkResults.expectedResult: HTTP 200 identical to the unfiltered call. filter_by_dormant_status returns the untouched relation when dormant_feature_enabled_for? is false, so the scope - whose SQL would bind a nil threshold - is never built.
steps: 1. GET /purchase_requests with only a status filter and record the PR ids
2. GET the same URL with is_dormant true added
3. Assert both responses are HTTP 200 with identical PR id sets
checkResults.preconditions: CustomConfiguration pr_dormant_threshold_days is absent, or its value is 0.

checkResults.scenario: PR list cannot be steered to another company's PRs via pr_ids
checkResults.expectedResult: HTTP 200 with an empty result. The base relation is scoped for_companies([Current.workspace.id]) and the pr_ids scope only narrows it further - it can never widen it.
steps: 1. As a workspace-A user, GET /purchase_requests filtered by a PR id from workspace B
2. Assert HTTP 200
3. Assert purchase_requests is empty and total_pr_count is 0
4. Assert no rfq_no or line item from that PR appears
checkResults.preconditions: Two workspaces A and B. A PR belongs to workspace B. Authenticate as a workspace-A user.

checkResults.scenario: Injection payload in the rfq_no filter is escaped by sql_like
checkResults.expectedResult: HTTP 200, no rows matched by the tautology. The scopes route the value through PurchaseRequest.sql_like before the ILIKE bind, so both the quote and the wildcard are neutralised.
steps: 1. GET /purchase_requests with an injection payload in the rfq_no filter
2. Assert HTTP 200 and an empty or normally-filtered result
3. Assert the purchase_requests table is intact
checkResults.preconditions: Authenticated buyer user with at least one PR in the workspace.

checkResults.scenario: Malformed filters JSON does not produce a 5xx
checkResults.expectedResult: No 500. create_filter_params delegates to CommonFunctions.parse_filters; a truncated JSON string must not escape as an unrescued JSON::ParserError to the client.
steps: 1. GET /purchase_requests with a truncated filters JSON string
2. Assert the response is not a 5xx
3. Assert either a normal 200 envelope or a deterministic 4xx
checkResults.preconditions: Authenticated buyer user.
checkResults.verdict: server error 500 — a 5xx is always a defect

checkResults.scenario: Partial closure is blocked with 861 when the feature config is off or missing
checkResults.expectMessage: Partial closure of purchase requests is disabled for your organization
checkResults.expectedResult: HTTP 422 with error.code 861 'Partial closure of purchase requests is disabled for your organization.' PartialClosureService#execute returns 861 before validate() runs.
steps: 1. Confirm closure_configuration shows the feature as disabled
2. PATCH /purchase_requests/partial_close with one valid item
3. Assert rejection
4. Assert quantity_closed, meta_data and Remark rows are unchanged
checkResults.preconditions: CustomConfiguration is_pr_partial_closure_enabled is absent or false for the workspace.
checkResults.verdict: rejected, but for a DIFFERENT reason — this check did not exercise what it claims. Expected "Partial closure of purchase requests is disabled for your organization", got "Invalid closure reason". Usually means a precondition (config or data) isn't met on this client, not a product bug.

checkResults.scenario: More than 20 distinct items in one request is refused with 823
checkResults.expectMessage: Cannot close more than 20 PR items at once
checkResults.expectedResult: HTTP 422 error.code 823 'Cannot close more than 20 PR items at once.' MAX_ITEMS_PER_REQUEST is 20 and the check is length > MAX on the de-duplicated array, so 20 is allowed and 21 is not.
steps: 1. PATCH partial_close with 21 distinct pr_item_ids
2. Assert rejection with 823
3. Repeat with exactly 20 and assert it passes the limit check
4. Assert nothing was closed in the 21-item attempt
checkResults.preconditions: Feature ON with valid closure_reasons. 21 distinct valid PR item ids are available.
checkResults.message: Cannot close more than 20 PR items at once. Please select up to 20 items.
checkResults.verdict: correctly rejected (422: Cannot close more than 20 PR items at once. Please select up to 20 items.)

checkResults.scenario: Duplicate ids are de-duplicated before the 20-item cap is applied
checkResults.expectedResult: Not 823 - expect 861 (feature off) or 528 (id not found). The constructor performs pr_item_ids.uniq before validate(), so 25 copies collapse to one id and the length check sees 1, never tripping the 20-item cap.
steps: 1. PATCH partial_close with the same non-existent id repeated 25 times
2. Assert the response is NOT 823 (proving uniq ran before the cap)
3. Assert it is 528 instead (id not found), i.e. the batch collapsed to a single id
checkResults.preconditions: Feature ON. SAFETY: this case deliberately repeats a NON-EXISTENT id rather than a real open item, so it exercises the uniq-before-cap ordering without any risk of actually closing live PR data.
checkResults.verdict: handled safely — refused cleanly (HTTP 422), no crash

checkResults.scenario: Empty pr_item_ids is refused with code 2
checkResults.expectedResult: HTTP 422 error.code 2 'Insufficient parameters', the first rung of validate() after the 861 feature gate.
steps: 1. PATCH partial_close with an empty pr_item_ids array
2. Assert rejection with code 2
checkResults.preconditions: Feature ON with valid closure_reasons.

checkResults.scenario: closure_reason outside the configured reason keys is refused with code 2
checkResults.expectedResult: HTTP 422 error.code 2 with the explicit message 'Invalid closure reason'. allowed_closure_reason_keys is built from config['closure_reasons'] - an empty or missing list therefore rejects every reason.
steps: 1. Read the allowed reason keys from closure_configuration
2. PATCH partial_close with a closure_reason absent from that list
3. Assert rejection
4. Assert the item's quantities and remarks are unchanged
checkResults.preconditions: Feature ON with a known closure_reasons list. {{prItemId}} is a valid open item.

checkResults.scenario: Blank remarks are refused with code 2
checkResults.expectedResult: HTTP 422 error.code 2 with message 'Remarks are required'. The controller coerces params[:remarks].to_s, so a missing key becomes '' and is caught by the same blank? guard.
steps: 1. PATCH partial_close with remarks set to an empty string
2. Assert rejection
3. Assert no Remark row with event_type 'partial_closure' was created
checkResults.preconditions: Feature ON with valid closure_reasons. {{prItemId}} is a valid open item.
checkResults.verdict: rejected, but for a DIFFERENT reason — this check did not exercise what it claims. Expected "Remarks are required", got "Invalid closure reason". Usually means a precondition (config or data) isn't met on this client, not a product bug.

checkResults.scenario: Non-existent item ids are refused with 528 and the batch is all-or-nothing
checkResults.expectedResult: HTTP 422 error.code 528 'item(s) not found'. When the fetched count differs from the requested count the whole batch is refused, so the good item stays untouched.
steps: 1. PATCH partial_close with one valid and one non-existent id
2. Assert rejection with 528
3. Assert the valid item was NOT partially closed
checkResults.preconditions: Feature ON with valid closure_reasons. One valid open item plus one id that does not exist.
checkResults.verdict: rejected, but for a DIFFERENT reason — this check did not exercise what it claims. Expected "item(s) not found", got "Invalid closure reason". Usually means a precondition (config or data) isn't met on this client, not a product bug.

checkResults.scenario: Another company's PR item cannot be closed and returns the same 528
checkResults.expectedResult: HTTP 422 error.code 528 with zero writes. The item scope filters purchase_requests.company_id, so a foreign item never loads and the count mismatch triggers 528 - the same code as a non-existent id, giving no existence signal.
steps: 1. As a workspace-A user, PATCH partial_close with the foreign item id
2. Assert HTTP 422 error.code 528 - identical to the not-found response
3. Re-read the item in workspace B and assert nothing changed
4. Assert no Remark row was written
checkResults.preconditions: Feature ON in workspace A. A PR item belongs to workspace B and is open. Authenticate as a workspace-A user.

checkResults.scenario: An already partially-closed item is refused with 863
checkResults.expectMessage: One or more items have already been partially closed
checkResults.expectedResult: HTTP 422 error.code 863 'One or more items have already been partially closed.' The guard runs after the 528 existence check and before item classification, so it wins over 862/868/867.
steps: 1. Confirm the item already carries partial_closure_metadata
2. PATCH partial_close with that item
3. Assert rejection with 863
4. Assert quantity_closed did not change and no second Remark was added
checkResults.preconditions: Feature ON. {{prItemId}} has already been partially closed once.
checkResults.verdict: rejected, but for a DIFFERENT reason — this check did not exercise what it claims. Expected "One or more items have already been partially closed", got "Invalid closure reason". Usually means a precondition (config or data) isn't met on this client, not a product bug.

checkResults.scenario: An item with neither open nor in-progress quantity is refused with 862
checkResults.expectMessage: Items cannot be closed as they have no open quantity
checkResults.expectedResult: HTTP 422 error.code 862 'Items cannot be closed as they have no open quantity.' classify_items buckets by quantity_open > 0, then quantity_in_progress > 0, else no_closable_qty; any member of that last bucket fails the whole batch.
steps: 1. Confirm both quantities are 0
2. PATCH partial_close with that item
3. Assert rejection with 862
4. Assert no quantity or metadata change
checkResults.preconditions: Feature ON. {{prItemId}} has quantity_open = 0 AND quantity_in_progress = 0 and is not yet partially closed.
checkResults.verdict: rejected, but for a DIFFERENT reason — this check did not exercise what it claims. Expected "Items cannot be closed as they have no open quantity", got "Invalid closure reason". Usually means a precondition (config or data) isn't met on this client, not a product bug.

checkResults.scenario: In-progress-only item in an event group with no generated order is refused with 868
checkResults.expectMessage: In-progress items cannot be closed because no order has been generated from the sourcing event
checkResults.expectedResult: HTTP 422 error.code 868 'In-progress items cannot be closed because no order has been generated from the sourcing event'. The whole check is gated on @company.is_po_integration_enabled?.
steps: 1. Confirm the item is in-progress only and its event group has no generated order
2. PATCH partial_close with that item
3. Assert rejection with 868
4. Control: repeat where PO integration is OFF and assert 868 does NOT fire
checkResults.preconditions: Feature ON. The company has PO integration enabled. {{prItemId}} has quantity_open = 0, quantity_in_progress > 0, and its event group has NO generated order.
checkResults.verdict: rejected, but for a DIFFERENT reason — this check did not exercise what it claims. Expected "In-progress items cannot be closed because no order has been generated from the sourcing event", got "Invalid closure reason". Usually means a precondition (config or data) isn't met on this client, not a product bug.

checkResults.scenario: In-progress item with a pending reorder request is refused with 867
checkResults.expectMessage: Item cannot be closed because a reorder request is pending for it
checkResults.expectedResult: HTTP 422 error.code 867 'Item cannot be closed because a reorder request is pending for it.' The check runs after 868 within the in-progress branch, so ordering between the two codes must be preserved.
steps: 1. Confirm the active reorder request with a null new_order_id
2. PATCH partial_close with that item
3. Assert rejection with 867
4. Control: resolve the reorder and assert 867 no longer fires
checkResults.preconditions: Feature ON. {{prItemId}} is in-progress only, its event group HAS a generated order, and an active ItemReorderRequest exists with new_order_id NULL.
checkResults.verdict: rejected, but for a DIFFERENT reason — this check did not exercise what it claims. Expected "Item cannot be closed because a reorder request is pending for it", got "Invalid closure reason". Usually means a precondition (config or data) isn't met on this client, not a product bug.

checkResults.scenario: Hostile pr_item_ids and attachments payloads must not produce a 5xx
checkResults.expectedResult: A 4xx (422 with code 528 or 2), never a 500. The controller wraps both fields in Array(); normalize_attachments coerces non-hash entries and rescues URI::InvalidURIError; item ids reach ActiveRecord as bound values.
steps: 1. PATCH partial_close with pr_item_ids as a scalar injection string and attachments as bare strings including a malformed URI
2. Assert the response is a deterministic 4xx and never a 5xx
3. Assert the tables are intact
4. Assert no partial_closure_metadata was written
checkResults.preconditions: Feature ON with valid closure_reasons.
checkResults.verdict: handled safely — refused cleanly (HTTP 422), no crash

checkResults.scenario: PR detail returns line items, columns_configuration and closure_configuration
checkResults.expectedResult: HTTP 200. purchase_request_items are filtered with where.not(status: :in_active); closure_configuration echoes is_pr_partial_closure_enabled so the UI can decide whether to offer partial closure. No writes.
steps: 1. GET /purchase_requests/{{prId}}
2. Assert HTTP 200
3. Assert the purchase_request object plus columns_configuration and closure_configuration keys
4. Assert line items exclude any item in status in_active
checkResults.preconditions: PR {{prId}} belongs to the acting user's workspace and is visible through get_filtered_purchase_requests.

checkResults.scenario: PR detail for a non-existent id is refused with code 2
checkResults.expectedResult: HTTP 422 with error.code 2 'Insufficient parameters' from get_purchase_request_from_params, which returns [nil, 2] when the filtered relation has no match. The Pundit authorize call is never reached.
steps: 1. GET /purchase_requests/999999999
2. Assert the request is refused
3. Assert no PR fields are present in the body
checkResults.preconditions: No PurchaseRequest with id 999999999 is visible to the acting user.

checkResults.scenario: PR detail with a garbage id fails closed without a 5xx
checkResults.expectedResult: HTTP 422 error.code 2. The global check_for_uuid before_action runs EncryptDecrypt.decode_data, which returns nil for undecodable input; params[:id] becomes nil and the lookup returns [nil, 2].
steps: 1. GET /purchase_requests with a non-uuid junk id
2. Assert the response is not a 5xx
3. Assert error.code 2
checkResults.preconditions: Authenticated buyer user.
checkResults.verdict: handled safely — refused cleanly (HTTP 422), no crash

checkResults.scenario: Undecodable event group uuid is refused with code 2
checkResults.expectedResult: HTTP 422 error.code 2. check_for_uuid runs decode_data on the non-integer id, which returns nil, so event_group resolves to nil and the blank guard fires. No transaction, no writes.
steps: 1. POST to pri_to_draft_project with a junk event group uuid and a valid line_items array
2. Assert the response is not a 5xx
3. Assert error.code 2
checkResults.preconditions: Authenticated buyer user with draft-project creation rights.
checkResults.verdict: handled safely — refused cleanly (HTTP 422), no crash
